title: LUCIND Study: Characterization of structural lung disease in children and adolescents with severe neurological diseases
summary: Children and adolescents with severe neurological diseases frequently suffer from respiratory problems. Causes often include swallowing difficulties or a weak cough, leading to retained secretions in the lungs. Little is currently known about how exactly these issues affect the structure of the lungs. In this study, we examine the lungs of these children once using a novel, very low-radiation computed tomography (photon-counting technology). We check for permanent damage such as widening of the airways or chronic inflammation. We also compare these images with medical data on swallowing ability and potential bacteria in the airways. The aim is to better understand risk factors in order to detect and treat lung problems in these children earlier and more specifically.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of a severe neurological disease (defined as CNS or neuromuscular disorder with severe motor/cognitive impairment)
- Assignable to one of three study groups: (1) Tracheostomy, (2) Dysphagia, (3) No Dysphagia
- Written informed consent obtained from patient and/or legal guardians
Exclusion criteria:
- Known primary pulmonary disease
- Acute severe illness
- Pregnancy
- Increased individual susceptibility to ionizing radiation
- Lack of informed consent
